title: Partial Kummer description of the inner-boundary unit after outer direct image
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ be a reduced strict normal crossings divisor with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and put $W=Y\setminus D$. Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization at a geometric point, with parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ cutting out the branches of $D$, $L$ becomes constant on the inverse-limit cover of the complement obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of all $t_i$ for every $n$ prime to $p$. This is the meaning of tame here; with no branches the cover is the identity. Write $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$, an ordinary tensor, for $F=E,\Omega$.

Partition $A=A_o\sqcup A_i$. Put $V=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_o}D_a$, $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $b:W\hookrightarrow V$, and let $h:Z_V\hookrightarrow V$ be the reduced closed complement of $W$ in $V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. All restrictions below are exact inverse images, with the coefficient identifications from pullback from the point. Put $K_F=Rb_{*,C_F}(L_F[0])$ and use the actual unit $\eta_{h,K_F}:K_F\to h_*h^*K_F$ of closed inverse/direct image [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Define the arrow
$$u_F=Rj_*(\eta_{h,K_F}):Rj_*Rb_*L_F[0]\longrightarrow Rj_*h_*h^*Rb_*L_F[0].$$
For $J\subseteq A$ with $J_i=J\cap A_i\ne\varnothing$, let $J_o=J\cap A_o$ and let $S_J=(\bigcap_{a\in J}D_a)\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin J}D_a$ with its reduced locally closed structure and inclusion $s_J:S_J\to Y$. Put $G_o=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^{J_o}$ and $G_i=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^{J_i}$, where $q$ runs over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/q^n\mathbf Z$. There is a pro-etale covering family $v_\alpha:T_\alpha\to S_J$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with simultaneous choices for $F=E,\Omega$ of compatible roots of unity and finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-representations $M_\alpha$ of $G_o\times G_i$, on which $(s_Jv_\alpha)^*u_F$ is identified with
$$p_{T_\alpha}^*\bigl(\theta_{M_{\alpha,F}}:R\Gamma_{G_o\times G_i}(M_{\alpha,F})\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{G_o}(R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}(M_{\alpha,F}))\bigr).$$
Here $M_{\alpha,F}$ is the condensed module $S\mapsto C(S,F\otimes_E M_\alpha)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. Equivariant module categories and inflation adjunctions are those of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]; $R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}$ derives $G_i$-invariants while retaining the $G_o$-action. All right derived functors are the ordinary K-injective ones [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The map $\theta$ is the right-derived composition comparison induced by $M^{G_o\times G_i}=(M^{G_i})^{G_o}$, equivalently the conjugate of composition of the exact inflation functors. The displayed identification specifies both objects and the arrow, not only the cohomology sheaves: the closed unit is sent to that comparison by the augmentation of the two partial Kummer nerves, adjoining inner roots first and outer roots second. It is natural in $L$ and under restriction of the covering family. No invertibility of $u_F$, no extension by zero, and no scalar-extension/direct-image commutation is part of this statement.

proof.text: Fix $J$ as in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-tame-root-tower-extension] with $I=J$. This supplies affine etale charts, affine pro-etale $U_\alpha$, their covering $T_\alpha=U_\alpha\times_Y S_J$ of the entire stratum, compatible roots of unity, and a deck-equivariant lisse extension $\widetilde L$ on the full root tower $\mathcal T$. Its boundary module is $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_\alpha$ with a continuous $E$-representation of $G_J$. Split the coordinates indexed by $J$ into $J_o,J_i$; reordering factors identifies $G_J=G_o\times G_i$. For $F=\Omega$ take $C_{\Omega,\mathcal T}\otimes_{C_{E,\mathcal T}}\widetilde L$. This remains lisse: on each finite free trivializing cover tensor sends $C_E^d$ to $C_\Omega^d$. Its restriction to the puncture is the actual pullback of $L_\Omega$, and its boundary module is $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,\Omega}$ by the same finite-basis computation. Thus the same covering and roots work for both $F$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the partial Kummer unit calculation; choice of common charts and equivariant extensions

proof.text: All work on $U_\alpha$ is restriction to a site slice: [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies its small pro-etale site with the slice of that of $Y$. The final slice clause of [lem-sfb-cech-localization-unit-totalization] permits this restriction of the direct-image calculation and of its unit, with the pulled-back rings. Let $\mathcal T^\circ\to W\times_YU_\alpha$ be the full root torsor. Its $n$th Cech term is $\mathcal T^\circ[(G_o\times G_i)^n]$ by the torsor identity in [lem-sfb-tame-root-tower-extension]. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-cech-image-totalization] to this cover and the composite $W\hookrightarrow Y$, followed by restriction to $T_\alpha$. Retain its compatible first-quadrant resolution as the coherent Cech model throughout the termwise comparisons below; totalization is applied to that model. For $P=(G_o\times G_i)^n$, [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity] computes this term as $p_{T_\alpha}^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_{\alpha,F})$. Its compatibility with profinite families of deck transformations identifies the first face with the action and the other faces with multiplication or deletion of the same coordinates. We therefore obtain the product derived internal bar, not merely its degreewise cohomology. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] its totalization is $p_{T_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_o\times G_i}(M_{\alpha,F})$. Pullback from the point commutes with these nonnegative total complexes degreewise, since each total degree has only finitely many summands. This calculation is made separately for each $F$ and does not use coefficient naturality to assert an isomorphism of derived scalar-comparison maps.

proof.text: For the target use $H=h_*h^*$ on $V$. Both factors are exact and the map $\mathrm{id}\to H$ is their actual adjunction unit by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Apply [lem-sfb-cech-localization-unit-totalization] with $f=b$, $g=j$, $t=s_Jv_\alpha$ and the full root cover of $W$. It identifies the restriction of $u_F=Rj_*(\eta_{h,Rb_*L_F})$ with the totalization of the same closed unit on the Cech terms. This application uses only $L_F[0]$ and nonnegative resolutions: $Rb_*$ and $Rj_*$ are left t-exact, so all resolution degrees remain nonnegative. In particular no assertion that $h^*$ sends injectives to injectives, and no interchange with an arbitrary unbounded product, is used. Derived direct-image composition and its canonical identifications follow also from [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], since the inverse-image functors are exact.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the partial Kummer unit calculation; transport of the actual closed unit through descent

proof.text: On the chart $U_\alpha$, $V$ inverts exactly the outer parameters and its reduced inner closed complement is the union where at least one inner parameter vanishes. This is exactly $V,Z,h$ of [lem-sfb-root-tower-inner-support]; it is the union, not the intersection of the inner components. For each root-nerve term let $f_P:\mathcal T^\circ[P]\to V\times_YU_\alpha$ be the structural map, so the $C_n$ in step 3 is $K_P=R(f_P)_*\widetilde L_F|_{\mathcal T^\circ[P]}[0]$. The support functor is applied on this base $V$, after $R(f_P)_*$; it is not moved through a ramified root morphism. Apply that node to the lisse extension from step 1 and each $P=(G_o\times G_i)^n$. Its equality $\sigma_P\circ s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_P})=\alpha_P$ identifies each term of the map from step 3 with the identity on the derived internal Hom term of step 2. Naturality for all profinite families is essential here: the first Cech face varies over the deck group. It makes these equalities equalities of cosimplicial diagrams. The source comparison is precisely $\alpha_P$ by [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity], so the target is identified with the same product-bar totalization, with the specified augmentation, rather than with an independently chosen isomorphic object.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the partial Kummer unit calculation; one-term inner-support calculation and unit equality

proof.text: Resolve the product root torsor in two stages. On the puncture, roots for inner coordinates and roots for outer coordinates satisfy separate equations, so adjoining the two sets successively gives the same algebra as adjoining them together: both are the quotient on the combined generators with the same power relations. The two deck actions commute. The associated double nerve has parameters $G_o^a\times G_i^b$; its diagonal reorders $(G_o\times G_i)^n$ as $G_o^n\times G_i^n$. Step 4 applies to these profinite parameters as well. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-product-bar-comparison] with $A=C_F$, $G=G_o$, $H=G_i$, $N=M_{\alpha,F}$. It identifies the target product-bar totalization with the iterated totalization (inner first, outer second), hence with $p_{T_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_o}R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}(M_{\alpha,F})$. Its augmentation normalization says that the map from step 4, after this target identification, is precisely $p_{T_\alpha}^*\theta_{M_{\alpha,F}}$. This proves both object identifications and the arrow identification of the question.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the partial Kummer unit calculation; two partial root nerves and product-to-iterated comparison

proof.text: For clarity this $\theta$ has exactly the definition in the statement. [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] identifies the composite exact inflations and their conjugate with $M^{G_o\times G_i}=(M^{G_i})^{G_o}$. [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] identifies its derived comparison on K-injective representatives with the class of this same identity, preserving the composite adjunctions. Thus the bar augmentation in step 5 has the prescribed ordinary K-injective normalization. To check a morphism $L\to L'$, refine the two chart covers by their fiber products, choose their two lisse extensions, and use [lem-sfb-root-tower-lisse-morphism-extension] to extend the actual puncture morphism uniquely on the full root tower. It is equivariant: for each deck action the two possible composites restrict to the same puncture map, and uniqueness gives equality; after each profinite base change this is the same uniqueness argument, so it is equivariance as a condensed-group morphism. Restricting to the boundary gives the map of $E$-representations. Ordinary scalar extension gives the map for $\Omega$. Now the naturality clauses for maps of supplied extensions in the support and acyclicity nodes, and naturality of Cech and bar descent, give commuting squares for every comparison. Their composite proves naturality in $L$. Refinements use the base-change clauses. Different extensions of a fixed puncture module are uniquely isomorphic by the same full-faithfulness statement, so these checks are independent of extension choices. The construction kept $F=E,\Omega$ on the same charts and used no scalar/direct-image interchange.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the partial Kummer unit calculation; normalization and naturality

proof.text: If $S_J$ is empty, use the empty covering family and the assertion has no members to check. If $J_o=\varnothing$, the outer group is trivial and its bar and invariants are the identity; the construction reduces to the inner nerve. The hypotheses require $J_i\ne\varnothing$, so there is no unsupported claim about an empty inner closed complement. Rank zero gives zero modules and zero complexes throughout. These checks also cover partitions with an empty outer part, and no strata of the stipulated type occur if the whole divisor or inner part is empty.
